item.title: Jail time for fatal crash
item.description: A MAN who admitted causing the death of his passenger after falling asleep behind the wheel of his vehicle was sentenced to 15 months’ imprisonment by the Rakiraki Magistrate’s Court. Waisake Sokomuri pleaded guilty to one count of dangerous driving occasioning death over a crash near Tavua on September 9, 2018.
item.content:encoded:
A MAN who admitted causing the death of his passenger after falling asleep behind the wheel of his vehicle was sentenced to 15 months’ imprisonment by the Rakiraki Magistrate’s Court.

Waisake Sokomuri pleaded guilty to one count of dangerous driving occasioning death over a crash near Tavua on September 9, 2018.

The court heard Sokomuri was driving a rental twin-cab from Lautoka to Tavua when he fell asleep about 200 metres from the Vutuna Junction, causing the vehicle to veer off the road into a drain.

Passenger Akuila Tuvulase sustained severe spinal injuries and was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit at Lautoka Hospital before dying on March 13, 2019. A post-mortem examination found the cause of death was sepsis and multiple pressure sores arising from injuries sustained in the crash.

Magistrate Timoci Qalinauci sentenced Sokomuri to 15 months’ imprisonment on June 30, ordering him to serve five months, with the remaining 10 months suspended for three years. He was also disqualified from driving for six months after completing his custodial sentence.

item.title: Assault leads to sentence
item.description: A 60-YEAR-OLD man as recently handed a wholly suspended prison sentence after admitting to unlawfully wounding his sister in a domestic violence incident in Ra. Magistrate Timoci Qalinauci in the Rakiraki Magistrate’s Court sentenced the man to 12 months’ imprisonment, suspended for three years.
item.content:encoded:
A 60-YEAR-OLD man as recently handed a wholly suspended prison sentence after admitting to unlawfully wounding his sister in a domestic violence incident in Ra.

Magistrate Timoci Qalinauci in the Rakiraki Magistrate’s Court sentenced the man to 12 months’ imprisonment, suspended for three years.

The court heard that on January 3, 2023, the man questioned his sister about her whereabouts before striking her buttocks and legs with an electric wire. The victim suffered discolouration to her back and buttocks.

The court also issued a permanent Domestic Violence Restraining Order protecting the victim for life and warned the man that breaching either the suspended sentence or the order could result in further charges.

item.title: Court rejects debt challenge
item.description: THE High Court recently struck out an application by 786 Hyper Mart Pte Ltd seeking to set aside a statutory demand issued by FMF Foods Ltd over an alleged debt of $33,819.58. Justice Chaitanya Lakshman ruled that the application was an abuse of the court process as the company did not dispute the debt owed to FMF Foods.
item.content:encoded:
THE High Court recently struck out an application by 786 Hyper Mart Pte Ltd seeking to set aside a statutory demand issued by FMF Foods Ltd over an alleged debt of $33,819.58.

Justice Chaitanya Lakshman ruled that the application was an abuse of the court process as the company did not dispute the debt owed to FMF Foods.

FMF Foods issued the statutory demand on February 18, 2026, after 786 Hyper Mart acknowledged a debt of $43,269.58 under a Deed of Acknowledgment of Debt entered into on January 30.

The court heard that 786 Hyper Mart made two payments of $5000 each, one on January 15 and another on February 9, but failed to make further payments.

FMF Foods then issued the statutory demand seeking payment of the outstanding amount, including interest.

Justice Lakshman noted that the purpose of a statutory demand was not to recover debts but to determine whether a company was solvent.

He said 786 Hyper Mart’s application was not based on a genuine dispute about the debt, but instead sought permission to repay the amount at a lower rate than agreed under the Deed of Acknowledgement of Debt.

The judge also found that an affidavit filed in support of the application was not properly authorised, as the person who purported to give authority to the company’s general manager was neither a director nor a secretary of the company.

Justice Lakshman struck out the originating summons and ordered 786 Hyper Mart to pay FMF Foods $2000 in costs within 21 days.

item.title: Visitor extensions top immigration applications
item.description: Visitor permit extension applications were the most common immigration applications lodged in Fiji between 2019 and 2023, while work permit applications recorded the highest number of refusals over the five-year period. Figures provided by the Fiji Immigration Department to the Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence, and tabled in Parliament, show that 19,101 visitor permit extension ap
item.content:encoded:
Visitor permit extension applications were the most common immigration applications lodged in Fiji between 2019 and 2023, while work permit applications recorded the highest number of refusals over the five-year period.

Figures provided by the Fiji Immigration Department to the Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence, and tabled in Parliament, show that 19,101 visitor permit extension applications were lodged between 2019 and 2023. Of these, 14,096 were approved and 5005 were refused.

Work permits recorded the second-highest number of applications, with 21,286 lodged over the five years.

Study permits ranked third, attracting 16,367 applications, with 15,342 approvals and just 733 refusals, giving them one of the highest approval rates.

Residence permit applications totalled 13,756, of which 10,434 were approved and 3326 refused.

Applications for single-entry visas reached 12,864, with 10,143 approvals and 2281 refusals.

Investor permits accounted for 2058 applications, with 1462 approved and 596 refused, while multiple-entry visas recorded 2158 applications, 1922 approvals, and the lowest number of refusals at 236.

The figures were included in information submitted by the Department of Immigration as part of the Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and Defence’s review process tabled in Parliament last month.

item.title: Rape charge fails, defilement proven
item.description: THE High Court in Labasa has acquitted a 20-year-old man of raping his 14-year-old neighbour but convicted him of the lesser charge of defilement and one of sexual assault. The man had pleaded not guilty to rape and sexual assault following an incident on April 24, 2025.
item.content:encoded:
THE High Court in Labasa has acquitted a 20-year-old man of raping his 14-year-old neighbour but convicted him of the lesser charge of defilement and one of sexual assault.

The man had pleaded not guilty to rape and sexual assault following an incident on April 24, 2025.

The court heard the man had sexual intercourse with the victim, a Year 8 student who has learning difficulties, while they were staying at a neighbour’s house.

During the trial, the victim admitted in cross-examination that she had consented to the sexual intercourse.

Consequently, Justice Lee James Burney ruled that the prosecution had failed to prove a lack of consent beyond a reasonable doubt, resulting in an acquittal on the rape charge.

However, Justice Burney found the man guilty of defilement. The court rejected the defence’s claim that the man reasonably believed the victim was 16 years old due to her physical build.

Justice Burney noted that the man knew the victim was a primary school student and a child.

item.title: Court grants FICAC application to amend charges against Biman Prasad
item.description: The Suva Magistrate’s Court has granted FICAC’s application to amend the charges against former Deputy Prime Minister Professor Biman Prasad. Magistrate Yogesh Prasad granted the application, stating that it was in the interest of justice.
item.content:encoded:
The Suva Magistrate’s Court has granted FICAC’s application to amend the charges against former Deputy Prime Minister Professor Biman Prasad.

Magistrate Yogesh Prasad granted the application, stating that it was in the interest of justice.

Professor Prasad will return to court at 2.30pm to take his plea on the amended charges.

Professor Prasad faces two charges relating to alleged failures to comply with statutory disclosure requirements in 2015, including the alleged omission of a directorship in a statutory declaration and providing false information.

Magistrate Prasad has vacated the initial four-day trial scheduled to begin this week and will refix the trial dates when the matter is recalled.

item.title: Tudravu stands by officer after Usamate challenges parking ticket
item.description: Commissioner of Police Rusiate Tudravu is standing by a traffic officer who issued a parking ticket to Opposition MP Jone Usamate, saying the officer was simply doing his job. Tudravu’s comments follow a social media post by Usamate describing the police action as an “overreach” after he received a parking ticket while carrying out parliamentary duties within the parliamentary precincts.
item.content:encoded:
Commissioner of Police Rusiate Tudravu is standing by a traffic officer who issued a parking ticket to Opposition MP Jone Usamate, saying the officer was simply doing his job.

Tudravu’s comments follow a social media post by Usamate describing the police action as an “overreach” after he received a parking ticket while carrying out parliamentary duties within the parliamentary precincts.

Usamate questioned the authority of police to issue the ticket within Parliament and called on the Minister responsible for policing and the Commissioner of Police to address the matter.

However, Commissioner Tudravu has defended the officer’s actions, saying the traffic infringement had been identified and the officer acted accordingly.

Tudravu said Usamate, like any other citizen, has the option of challenging the decision in a court of law if he believes the ticket was wrongly issued.

The Commissioner said he was standing by the officer’s action and maintained that the officer was carrying out his responsibility in enforcing traffic laws.

He also urged members of the public who have concerns about the conduct of police officers to use the proper reporting and complaints channels.

item.title: Chand tells Education Ministry: Stop excuses, pay teachers
item.description: Opposition MP Hem Chand has called on the Ministry of Education to take responsibility for delays in paying teachers, saying administrative problems should not result in educators going without salaries they have already earned. Chand said teachers and their families should not have to bear the consequences of delays within the Ministry.
item.content:encoded:
Opposition MP Hem Chand has called on the Ministry of Education to take responsibility for delays in paying teachers, saying administrative problems should not result in educators going without salaries they have already earned.

Chand said teachers and their families should not have to bear the consequences of delays within the Ministry.

“How long must our teachers continue to wait for the salaries they have rightfully earned?” Chand asked.

“The Ministry of Education must stop hiding behind excuses and take responsibility for the unacceptable delays in paying teachers.”

His comments follow confirmation from the Ministry that salary arrears owed to 318 staff members would be paid under Pay 17 and Pay 18.

Education Minister Aseri Radrodro had said common issues identified in processing arrears included the absence of Fiji Teachers Registration Authority registration certificates, missing bank details and delays in confirmation of officers commencing duties from Heads of Schools or District Education Officers.

Chand rejected those issues as sufficient justification for prolonged salary delays.

“Excuses such as missing FTRA registration certificates or bank details cannot justify teachers being left without their salaries for months,” he said.

“If there are administrative problems, the Ministry must fix them urgently rather than allowing teachers and their families to bear the consequences of bureaucratic failures.”

Chand said teachers were simply seeking payment for work they had already performed.

“Teachers are not asking for a favour. They are asking for what they have already earned,” he said.

He also questioned the Coalition Government’s commitment to supporting educators when some teachers were experiencing salary delays.

“The Coalition Government has repeatedly spoken about improving education and supporting our teachers. But what message are we sending when hardworking teachers cannot even receive their salaries on time?”

“Teachers’ welfare must be a priority — not an afterthought.”

Chand called on the Education Minister to ensure all outstanding salaries were settled without further delay.

“I call on the Minister for Education to stop the excuses, take responsibility and ensure that all outstanding teacher salaries are paid immediately,” he said.

He also called on Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka to personally intervene and seek an urgent resolution.

“A government that values education must value the people who deliver it,” Chand said.

“Our teachers deserve dignity. Our teachers deserve respect. Our teachers deserve to be paid on time.”

Chand concluded his statement with a direct demand: “Enough of the excuses. Enough of the delays. Pay our teachers — now!”
